correctness.rationale: All 2^16 local edge-pairings of the complete order-four de Bruijn graph are exhaustively enumerated, and the single-cycle condition is equivalent to an Eulerian de Bruijn tour. An independent edge-distinct Eulerian DFS yields the identical 2048 rotation classes, all directly tested for one occurrence of each five-bit factor. Standard interval recurrences with rigorously derived endpoint cases calculate exact longest ordinary and antipalindromic subsequences for each of 32 cuts; an independently programmed LCS method agrees on every one of 65536 cuts. The complete per-cycle data and source checker reproduce 19 joint frequencies totaling 2048, marginals, and symmetry orbits. Only the finite order-five theorem is asserted.

value.rationale: The two joint coordinates are precisely the paired longest scattered-subsequence invariants introduced as natural circular-word extremal problems by Müllner–Ryzhikov, motivated by the Lyngsø–Pedersen balanced-circle problem. De Bruijn cycles form the canonical uniformly balanced, locally universal subclass. The exact conditional spectrum exposes a nontrivial tradeoff—perfect reverse-complement-palindromic cuts are incompatible with maximum ordinary palindrome length 29—and sharp simultaneous near-optimal deletion counts. The 19-cell population classification is not determined by the known ordinary marginal, existing reverse-complement symmetry results, or general lower bounds. A natural exact finite classification is meaningful even without an all-order theorem.
